stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "path": "memory/continual-arc-task-524afec6.md",
 "content": "# Task 524afec6 — opposite-edge bars and marker-driven fill

Verified with two demonstrations and the accepted test submission.

## Rule
Two equal-length straight boundary bars of a background/boundary color occupy separate, aligned bands on opposite edges of the grid (one on the left, one on the right; demos also show analogous horizontal bands). A sparse marker of a different color occurs within one band. Use the marker color to fill:

1. In the marker's own row, extend from the marker toward the opposing edge boundary, replacing the marker itself with color 4.
2. In the opposite bar's corresponding row (same offset within its bar), fill the whole intervening span between that bar and the far edge, with the marker color.
3. For multiple marker rows, apply both operations for each; leave rows with no corresponding marker unchanged. Preserve the boundary bars and all unrelated cells.

For the accepted test, color-9 bars were at left column rows 0–5 and right column rows 10–15. An 8 marker at (row 14, col 6) was changed to 4; row 14 was filled with 8 from col 7 through col 21, and corresponding row 4 was filled with 8 from col 1 through col 22. Submission was accepted.

## Demo confirmation
- Demo 1: color-2 bars at right col 7, rows 0–13, and left col 0, rows 14–27. Color-1 markers in the lower bar's rows selected corresponding rows of the upper bar; each marker row in the lower band was filled from just inside the left boundary through the marker, with the marker changed to 4. The matching row of the upper band was filled fully up to its right boundary. Rows without markers stayed unchanged.
- Demo 2: color-7 bars along top row cols 0–1 and bottom row cols 2–3. Color-3 markers at (5,3) and (10,2) were changed to 4; filling propagated from the marker boundary into the aligned opposite span, yielding the stepped filled region in the output.

Interpret aligned offsets within the separate boundary bands; do not fill every row indiscriminately. Preserve all bar cells.
